title: Self-Healing Infrastructure
brief: System automatically detects drift, repairs itself, and adapts thresholds with zero manual maintenance. Auto-repair schema drift (z.enum vs exports), auto-sync registries (SKILL_INDEX vs actual), auto-validate hook configs, auto-prune stale memory, auto-quarantine flaky tests, adaptive safety limits from 910-machine catalog, cache TTL auto-tuning via gradient descent, Python hook health monitor with auto-restart, atomicWrite race condition fix with OS-level locks, pipeline rollback on mid-stage failure, Bayesian-optimized dedup windows.

phases.title: Self-Healing Systems
phases.description: Build automatic detection and repair for schema drift, registry staleness, hook config errors, memory bloat, flaky tests, safety limit drift, cache TTL mis-tuning, Python hook failures, file write races, pipeline mid-failure recovery, and dedup window optimization.

units.title: Schema drift auto-repair
units.rationale: z.enum lists in dispatchers frequently drift from actual engine exports. A cron scanning exports vs z.enum every 12h and auto-patching mismatches eliminates a top-3 build failure cause.
exit_conditions: Cron runs every 12h scanning engine exports vs z.enum

steps.instruction: Build scanner: parse all dispatcher z.enum lists and all engine index.ts exports.
Diff: identify entries in z.enum but not exported (orphans) and exported but not in z.enum (missing).
Auto-patch: add missing entries to z.enum, remove orphans, preserving alphabetical order.
Generate diff report: what changed, when, why.
Set up 12h cron via CronCreate.
Test with intentionally introduced drift.

deliverables.description: Schema drift scanner and auto-repair cron

units.title: Registry drift auto-sync
units.rationale: SKILL_INDEX, agent_registry, ENGINE_DIGEST, and DISPATCHER_DIGEST can go stale when engines/skills are added. A 12h cron comparing these registries against actual files and auto-regenerating stale ones keeps the system self-consistent.
exit_conditions: Cron runs every 12h comparing registries vs actual files

steps.instruction: Build comparator: count engines in src/engines/ vs ENGINE_DIGEST, dispatchers in src/dispatchers/ vs DISPATCHER_DIGEST.
Compare SKILL_INDEX entries against actual .md files in commands/.
Compare agent_registry entries against actual agent configs.
Auto-regenerate any stale registry using existing generator scripts.
Set up 12h cron; test with intentionally stale registry.

units.title: Hook config auto-validate
units.rationale: Hook config errors (bad regex matchers, missing script files, syntax errors) cause silent failures. SessionStart validation catches these before they cause issues during the session.
features: syntax error detection in hook scripts
exit_conditions: All hook scripts validated for syntax errors at SessionStart

steps.instruction: Parse .claude/settings.local.json to enumerate all hook configurations.
For each hook: validate script file exists, check bash/python syntax, test matcher regex compiles.
For each referenced file in hook scripts (source, import): verify existence.
Wire into session-start-unified; surface warnings for any issues found.
Test with intentionally broken hook config.

units.title: Memory auto-prune
units.rationale: MEMORY.md grows unboundedly with references to files that may have been deleted or moved. SessionEnd pruning of stale refs and auto-archiving keeps memory under 180 lines and contextually relevant.
exit_conditions: MEMORY.md scanned for stale file references

steps.instruction: Parse MEMORY.md for file path references (backtick paths, markdown links).
Check each referenced path for existence; flag missing as stale.
Move stale entries to memory-archive.md with timestamp.
If line count > 180, identify lowest-value entries (oldest, least referenced) and archive.
Test with MEMORY.md containing known stale refs.

units.title: Test flakiness quarantine
units.rationale: Flaky tests erode trust in the test suite and waste investigation time. Tracking per-test pass/fail over last 20 runs and quarantining when P(flaky)>0.1 keeps the suite reliable while preserving test coverage.
exit_conditions: Per-test pass/fail tracked over last 20 runs

steps.instruction: Build test result parser: extract per-test pass/fail from vitest JSON output.
Persist per-test results in ~/.prism/test-history.json (rolling 20 runs).
Compute P(flaky) = count(alternating pass/fail) / total_runs per test.
Quarantine: add .skip to tests with P(flaky)>0.1; log issue.
Restore: remove .skip when P(flaky)<0.02 over next 20 runs.
Test with intentionally flaky test.

units.title: Adaptive safety limits
units.rationale: Fixed 60K RPM / 50K mm/min safety limits are overly conservative for low-speed machines and insufficient for high-speed spindles. Using the 910-machine catalog to set machine-specific limits is both safer and less restrictive.
exit_conditions: Safety limits derived from machine-specific catalog data
Each machine gets its own max RPM/feed
Unknown machines fall back to conservative defaults

steps.instruction: Extract max_spindle_speed and max_feed_rate from all 910 machine profiles.
Replace fixed 60K/50K constants with machine-specific lookups.
Add 10% safety margin: limit = catalog_max * 0.9.
Fallback: if machine not in catalog, use conservative P10 of all machines.
Test with high-speed (80K RPM) and low-speed (6K RPM) machines.

units.description: Adaptive safety limits — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: Cache TTL auto-tuning
units.rationale: Fixed cache TTLs cannot adapt to changing data patterns. Weekly gradient descent on P(stale) targeting <=0.01 automatically finds the optimal TTL per cache, balancing freshness against hit rate.
entry_conditions: CCM-MS14 P0-U06 cache monitor providing hit/miss/stale data
exit_conditions: Cache TTLs auto-tuned weekly via gradient descent

steps.instruction: Collect weekly cache metrics from CCM-MS14 P0-U06: hit rate, miss rate, stale rate per cache.
Implement gradient descent: dP(stale)/dTTL approx from finite differences; step TTL to minimize |P(stale)-0.01|.
Constraints: TTL_min=1s, TTL_max=3600s; learning rate 0.1 with decay.
Apply optimized TTLs; log old vs new TTL and expected P(stale).
Set up weekly cron; test convergence on simulated cache data.

units.description: Cache TTL auto-tuning — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: Python hook health monitor
units.rationale: Python hooks (syntax check, linting) can silently die. A 60s heartbeat with P(available) tracking and auto-restart after 3 failures ensures Python hook reliability with TS fallback.
exit_conditions: Python hook health monitored with 60s heartbeat
Fallback to TS equivalent when Python unavailable

steps.instruction: Implement heartbeat: every 60s, run python --version and a trivial syntax check.
Track P(available) = successes / (successes + failures) over rolling window.
On 3 consecutive heartbeat failures: kill and restart Python process.
If restart fails: switch to TS-based syntax checker as fallback.
Test with simulated Python process death.

units.title: atomicWrite race fix
units.rationale: The current .tmp+rename atomicWrite pattern can race when multiple hooks write to the same file concurrently. OS-level advisory locks (flock on Linux/WSL, LockFileEx on Windows) eliminate this race condition.
exit_conditions: Lock timeout with retry prevents deadlocks

steps.instruction: Identify all atomicWrite call sites across hook scripts.
Implement lock wrapper: flock on Linux/WSL, PowerShell LockFileEx on Windows.
Add timeout (5s) with exponential backoff retry (3 attempts).
Replace all .tmp+rename patterns with locked write.
Stress test: 10 concurrent writers to same file.

units.title: Pipeline rollback on failure
units.rationale: PrintToProgramPipeline currently loses all work on mid-stage failure. Checkpointing per stage and rolling back to N-1 on stage N failure preserves partial results and enables retry from last good state.
exit_conditions: Pipeline checkpoints state after each stage
On stage N failure, rolls back to stage N-1 output

steps.instruction: Identify all pipeline stages in PrintToProgramPipeline and PostProcessorPipeline.
Implement checkpoint: serialize stage output to ~/.prism/pipeline-checkpoints/{run_id}/{stage_id}.json.
On stage failure: log error, load checkpoint from stage N-1, return partial result.
Add retry-from-checkpoint API: resume pipeline from any checkpointed stage.
Auto-prune checkpoints older than 24h.
Test with simulated mid-pipeline failure and recovery.

units.description: Pipeline rollback on failure — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: Adaptive dedup windows
units.rationale: Building on CCM-MS14 P0-U02 Beta distributions and P0-U10 FP tracking, Bayesian optimization finds the window that minimizes weighted FP+missed cost per tool, with different cost weights reflecting tool expense.
entry_conditions: CCM-MS14 P0-U02 and P0-U10 providing FP/FN data
exit_conditions: Dedup windows auto-tuned via Bayesian optimization

steps.instruction: Define cost model: FP_cost (blocked needed call) vs missed_cost (allowed duplicate) per tool type.
Implement Bayesian optimization: GP surrogate on (window_ms) -> total_cost, EI acquisition.
Use CCM-MS14 P0-U02 Beta posteriors as prior; update with P0-U10 FP data.
Run optimization weekly; apply new windows; log changes.
Test convergence on synthetic cost data.

units.title: Self-healing integration tests
units.rationale: Each self-healing subsystem needs integration testing to verify it actually repairs the problem it detects. Simulating schema drift, cache corruption, hook failure, and pipeline mid-failure then verifying auto-repair provides confidence in the self-healing infrastructure.
exit_conditions: Integration tests pass for all 11 self-healing subsystems
Each test: introduce fault, verify detection, verify auto-repair

steps.instruction: Test schema drift: remove 3 z.enum entries, run repair cron, verify restored.
Test registry drift: delete ENGINE_DIGEST, run sync cron, verify regenerated.
Test hook config: introduce syntax error, verify SessionStart catches it.
Test memory prune: add refs to nonexistent files, verify auto-archived.
Test cache corruption: write invalid JSON to cache file, verify auto-recovery.
Test pipeline rollback: inject failure at stage 3, verify checkpoint at stage 2 used.
Run all tests in sequence; verify no cross-contamination.

deliverables.description: Integration tests for all self-healing subsystems
